notes: San Francisco Bay Guardian, 1977 to 1986, the 127 issues the Internet Archive collection holds for those years (none for 1980), read from its DjVu text. Hand-curated: article passages were read and each finding's quote checked against the issue. People rule as in the dossier: no owners, staff, tenants, performers or customers.

coverage.remaining: 696 issues, 1988 to 2014: next 1988–1994 (179 issues), then 1998–2006 (122) and 2008–2014 (395, lower value: those years were on the open web).
coverage.note: 127 issues; 33,064 numbered-address mentions on EAS streets, of which the advertisement filter marked 27,981 and kept 1,381 windows in 1,088 address clusters. Read: the 80 clusters of article prose (all), the 16 event-word passages left by the tighter filter (all), and a new pass over the raw text, outside the advertisement filter, for prose that holds a numbered address and a building-news word (news.py: 55 passages, all read). About 35 candidates were checked against the issue text; 26 were written and 5 dropped at the overlap check as already on their pages (the Crocker Bank landmark fight at 1 Sansome, 101 Mission's approval, the Mining Exchange at 350 Bush, the firehouse at 466 Bush, the Coltrane church at 351 Divisadero). 21 findings, each quote found again in the issue's text. 15 resolved and published on 15 pages, none seeded; 1 of them placed by hand (the Audiffred Building, printed as 9 Mission Street, on its page at 1 Mission). 2 held as single facts on parcels with no page (1660 Bush and 3410 19th). 4 unresolved at numbers EAS no longer holds: 842 Kearny (the Victory Building), 128 The Embarcadero, 58-64 Sutter and 22 Kearny. The audit flags 2 of 21: the Clayton Hotel's price, which the scan prints as '$1,3 million', and 100 First Street's 450,000 square feet, printed further on in the story than the audit looks. The issues grow to 100 pages and more in these years, almost all of it listings and advertising; the yield per issue is lower than in 1966–1976.

findings.description: Five-day eviction notices were posted on 5 December 1977 at the Victory Building, 842 Kearny Street, next door to the International Hotel and owned by the same corporation. It had once housed as many as 50 elderly Chinese and Filipino residents; the three who remained agreed to leave by 27 December, and the senior citizens' center downstairs, which served meals to a couple of hundred people a day, had to move as well.
